title: Weights & Caches: LLMs Can Program Tabular Foundation Models
read_level: full main text and appendices A-B; appendix C (KV-cache) skimmed
metadata_mismatch: minor: metadata spells 'Magnus Buehler', paper spells 'Magnus Bühler'
why_wsp: GPT-6 Astra writes nanoTabPFN weights from zero, edits pretrained TabPFN-3.5 weights to repair a signed-product regression failure, and writes KV-cache editing programs, all without gradient optimization.
domain: tabular foundation models (TabPFN-3.5, nanoTabPFN); tabular classification/regression
editor: GPT-6 Astra (gpt-6-astra, via Codex CLI for the repair setting)
target: nanoTabPFN ("116 tensors and 3,717,514 weights"), pretrained TabPFN-3.5 (official checkpoint tabpfn-v3.5-20260909); KV-cache of TabPFN-3.5 (weights frozen)
interface: code/tensor tools (agent writes weights via Python code; closed-form fits allowed in repair; Python edit(cache) function for steering)
loop: construct: one-shot (no forward passes allowed); repair: closed-loop with feedback (3 validation feedback requests); steer: closed-loop exploration on dev datasets
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Construct: "Nonzero weights 15,513 (0.42%)" (App. A Table 2). Repair: "Changed tensors / weight entries 125 / approximately 105 million" (App. B Table 4); "it does not establish that a small local edit suffices" (App. B).

headline_results.quote: achieving a mean ROC AUC of 0.849 across 20 TabArena datasets, compared to 0.876 for a pretrained baseline
log loss of 0.397 on the 20 datasets, compared to 0.876 and 0.312 for the pretrained baseline
WSP-NanoTabPFN has the higher AUC on 3 of the 20 datasets
the repair raises median per-dataset R2 from −0.024–0.017 to 0.991–0.998 on held-out synthetic datasets
geometric-mean edited-to-pretrained error ratio is 1.0008 (95% confidence interval: 0.9999–1.0017)
Both programs approximate the intended transformations on previously unseen datasets, although the quality of the interventions varies across datasets.

cost.where: App. A Table 2 (7 turns, 5 Python runs)

cost.quote: Wall-clock time / allowed budget ... 62 min / 5 h
Astra took about 20 minutes to write the slope program and 70 minutes to write the square-wave program

baselines_and_controls: Construct: nanoTabPFN pretrained on 160,000 synthetic tables (SGD baseline). Repair: unedited pretrained TabPFN-3.5 on signed-product and TabArena-Lite; agent control reserving coordinates without activating sign output "leaves performance near chance". No random-edit or fine-tuning baseline.
runs_and_variance: Construct: "We ran two sessions under this protocol and report the better one" (App. A). Repair: one agent session; TabArena-Lite errors averaged over three seeds with 95% CI. 60 hidden datasets per regime.
robustness_of_edits: Repair: "Transfer beyond the targeted regimes is partial" (App. B); reload of merged checkpoint reproduces scores on all 240 hidden datasets. Not tested under fine-tuning or quantization.
verification: none formal; statistical preservation criteria with preset limits; transcript audit: "We audited the recorded transcripts and programs for compliance with these rules and found no violations." (Sec. 3)
memorization_vs_reasoning: Construct: Astra "implements a multiscale kernel naive Bayes classifier" rather than reproducing pretrained weights, with no data or forward passes. Repair diagnosis based on linear probes; authors note results "do not establish that the pretrained model already contained the complete circuit".
limitations_stated: Findings "remain exploratory" (Sec. 4); repair changes ~105M entries, not a small local edit; transfer beyond targeted regimes partial; KV-steering quality varies across datasets.
code_or_data: none found (no code URL in paper; baseline prior from https://github.com/automl/TFM-Playground/)
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026, Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog)
notes_for_survey: Spans B2 (write TFM from zero, no forward passes, 0.42% nonzero), B3 (diagnose-then-repair via probes, ~105M entries changed) and a KV-cache variant (weights frozen). The construct result reports best of two sessions.
